models.name: Affordable buff-brick bay-window bungalow
models.brief: A modest low buff-brick bungalow with one small projecting front bay window, one front door to its right, a shallow grey-brown tiled hip roof and one rear-left chimney. No garage, no extra wings, no columns. Different low compact silhouette from the first1990sredbrick garage house.

models.name: Affordable single-storey redbrick duplex
models.brief: Two compact side-by-side one-storey redbrick homes under one shared charcoal pitched roof. Exactly two front doors near the middle, two broad outer front living windows, separate rear GLASS patio sliders, two roof vents. No upstairs floor or garage. An ordinary affordable duplex, distinct from the two-storey2010stownhouse pair.

models.name: Small affordable six-flat walk-up
models.brief: A modest rectangular three-storey six-flat walk-up: brick lower storey, cream upper render, shallow flat parapet roof, ONE shared central front entrance, two small balconies per floor (six total) with plain metal rails, fixed rear/end window grids, one rear service door. No tower, lifts in glass shafts, luxury roof terraces or giant glazing. Dwelling count is an art/design proposal, never game population balance.

models.name: Compact two-storey gabled solar family home
models.brief: Affordable compact two-storey family infill home: white lower walls, charcoal upper front/rear cladding, one ordinary pitched gable roof, timber front door with a narrow side-light, broad front living window, rear GLASS patio slider and FOUR solar modules in two rows of two ONLY on the fixed front roof slope. Rear roof does not acquire the solar panels when turned. No garage, flat-roof sci-fi shapes or mansion scale.
